title: Establish tiered SLOs and rollout gates for async batch embeddings with capacity-aware error-budget reallocation
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description: PRD summary: Define explicit SLO bands, uptime targets and error budgets for asynchronous batch embeddings pipelines. Include phased rollout gates tied to capacity availability windows, error-budget reallocation mechanics (to borrow capacity from low-priority tenants during bursts), and acceptance criteria for automated rollback. This ticket clarifies requirements, measurable targets, and operational playbooks for safe deployments of batching/throughput improvements that change latency distributions.
background: We are introducing new batching heuristics and priority-aware scheduling in the embeddings runner to reduce per-unit cost. These changes shift service behavior for batched workloads: bulk jobs may see longer tail latencies during tight capacity windows but overall throughput improves. To safely release, we need a PRD-level contract that states acceptable latency envelopes, how to allocate/deplete error budgets per tier, and deterministic gates for canary and fleet rollouts.
goals: Define P50/P95/P99 latency envelopes for three tenant priority tiers (realtime, standard, background) for batch embedding jobs
Specify uptime targets and allowable scheduled maintenance windows for batch processing nodes
Design error-budget accounting and temporary reallocation policy to allow borrowing unused error budget from background tier to sustain realtime during bursts
Establish rollout gates with metric thresholds, burn-rate checks, and automated rollback criteria
Provide clear acceptance criteria and test harness requirements for runtime/observability teams
success_metrics: Realtime batch P95 <= 1.5s per item during normal load (measured downstream of batching) with <1% violation weekly
Standard tier P95 <= 3.0s per item with <2% weekly violations
Background tier P95 <= 10s per item; allowed to absorb >90% of burst tail
System-wide embedding throughput improves by >=18% on sample workloads compared to baseline
No customer-facing errors introduced by rollout (failed jobs retryable and error rate increase <0.1% absolute)
acceptance_criteria: Performance characterization report with synthetic and production-like traces demonstrating metrics above across 2 test regions
Automated canary that runs representative batch jobs and validates SLOs over a 48h window before ramping
Monitoring alerts and dashboards instrumented: per-tenant latency histograms, per-priority error-budget burn rate, and capacity headroom gauges
Rollback playbook documented and tested: automated rollback triggers on burn-rate > 3x baseline or P99 regressions > 20% sustained for 30m
Integration tests validating error-budget reallocation flows with mocked multi-tenant traffic patterns
rollout_gates: Stage 0 (Canary): 1% of traffic, 48h observation, burn-rate <1.5x and no P99 degradation >10%
Stage 1 (Limited): 10% of traffic with adaptive slow-start over 6h, error-budget borrow disabled
Stage 2 (Tiered Rollout): enable error-budget reallocation for background -> realtime with strict quotas and audit logs; run for 72h
Stage 3 (Full): remove restrictions if sustained stability for 7d and cost/throughput metrics meet targets
monitoring_and_alerts: SLO dashboards: P50/P95/P99 per priority tier, aggregated and per-tenant
Burn-rate alert: triggers at 1.5x baseline (warning) and 3x (critical)
Capacity headroom alert when active queue depth > 75% of safe limit for >10m
Automated incident ticket creation with pre-populated playbook links when critical alerts fire
tradeoffs_and_risks: Allowing background tier to borrow error budget reduces cost but risks degraded background job latency and potential SLA complaints
More aggressive batching yields better throughput and lower unit cost but amplifies tail latency — must balance with tenant priorities
Automated reallocations need strict auditing to avoid silent performance regressions for paying customers
decisions_needed: Define concrete quotas for borrowed error budget (absolute vs percentage) per tenant class
Agree retention period for audit logs produced by reallocations
Decide whether to expose per-tenant opt-out for borrowing policy
